spec.title: Reading Status
spec.description: How healthy is the fleet right now?

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
    status,
    ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct
FROM iiot.iot_data
WHERE $__timeFilter("timestamp") 
GROUP BY status
ORDER BY status DESC;

spec.title: Critical events by day of week
spec.description: Critical events by hour — spot operational patterns

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
    EXTRACT(DOW FROM "timestamp") AS day_of_week_number,
    date_format('%a', "timestamp") AS day_of_week,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'critical') AS "Critical Error Count"
FROM iiot.iot_data
WHERE  $__timeFilter("timestamp") 
GROUP BY day_of_week,day_of_week_number
ORDER BY day_of_week_number;

spec.title: Critical alerts on out-of-warranty assets
spec.description: iot_data + devices  →  find exposed assets that need budget attention

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
    d.device_id AS "Device ID",
    d.manufacturer AS "Manufacturer",
    d.device_type AS "Device Type",
    d.warranty_expiry AS "Warranty Expiry",
    d.asset_value_eur AS "Asset Value €",
    COUNT(*)           AS "Critical Readings",
    MAX(i."timestamp") AS "Last Critical at"
FROM iiot.iot_data i
JOIN iiot.devices d ON i.device_id = d.device_id
WHERE i.status = 'critical'
  AND d.warranty_expiry < TIMESTAMP '2025-09-01'
GROUP BY d.device_id, d.manufacturer, d.device_type, d.warranty_expiry, d.asset_value_eur
ORDER BY "Critical Readings" DESC
LIMIT 15;

spec.title: Overdue maintenance
spec.description: iot_data + devices  →  devices past their scheduled service date and still active

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
    d.device_id AS "Device ID",
    d.device_type AS "Device Type",
    initcap(replace(d.plant_id,'PLANT_','')) AS "Plant ID",
    d.responsible_technician AS "Responsible Technician",
    d.next_maintenance_due AS "Next Maintenance Due",
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.status IN ('warning', 'critical')) AS "Fault Readings"
FROM iiot.iot_data i
JOIN iiot.devices d ON i.device_id = d.device_id
WHERE d.next_maintenance_due < TIMESTAMP '2025-09-01'
GROUP BY d.device_id, d.device_type, d.plant_id, d.responsible_technician, d.next_maintenance_due
ORDER BY "Fault Readings" DESC
LIMIT 15;

spec.title: Devices still faulting after maintenance
spec.description: iot_data + devices + maintenance_log  →  maintenance that did not hold

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
    i.device_id AS "Device ID",
    d.manufacturer AS "Manufacturer",
    d.device_type AS "Device Type",
    m.maintenance_type AS "Maintenance Type",
    m.completed_date AS "Completed Date",
    m.cost_eur AS "Cost €",
    COUNT(*) AS "Fault Readings After Service"
FROM iiot.iot_data i
JOIN iiot.devices d          ON i.device_id = d.device_id
JOIN iiot.maintenance_log m  ON i.device_id = m.device_id
WHERE i.status IN ('warning', 'critical')
  AND m.status = 'completed'
  AND i."timestamp" > m.completed_date::TIMESTAMP
GROUP BY i.device_id, d.manufacturer, d.device_type,
         m.maintenance_type, m.completed_date, m.cost_eur
ORDER BY "Fault Readings After Service" DESC
LIMIT 10;

spec.title: Overall Equipment Effectiveness
spec.description:
Overall Equipment Effectiveness derived from sensor status and quality_score.
-- This is an approximation — a full OEE calculation requires a shift_production
-- table with runtime, planned time, actual output, and good units. Using the
-- fields available in iot_data:
--   Availability = share of readings where device was online (status != 'offline')
--   Performance  = share of online readings in normal operating state
--   Quality      = average quality_score of online readings, normalised to 0–1
--   OEE          = Availability × Performance × Quality × 100

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
    p.plant_name AS "Plant Name",
    p.industry_segment AS "Industry Segment",
    i.device_type AS "Device Type",
    COUNT(*)                                                         AS "Total Readings",
    ROUND(
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.status != 'offline') * 100.0
        / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1
    )                                                                AS "Availability %",
    ROUND(
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.status = 'normal') * 100.0
        / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.status != 'offline'), 0), 1
    )                                                                AS "Performance %",
    ROUND(
        AVG(i.quality_score) FILTER (WHERE i.status != 'offline'), 1
    )                                                                AS "Quality Score Avg",
    ROUND(
          (COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.status != 'offline')    * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0))
        * (COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.status = 'normal')      * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.status != 'offline'), 0))
        * (AVG(i.quality_score) FILTER (WHERE i.status != 'offline') / 100.0)
        * 100, 1
    )                                                                AS "Oee Approx %"
FROM iiot.iot_data i
JOIN iiot.plants p ON i.plant_id = p.plant_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(i."timestamp") 
GROUP BY i.plant_id, p.plant_name, p.industry_segment, i.device_type
ORDER BY "Oee Approx %" ASC;

SELECT query_name, search_string "Search String"
FROM "iiot"."knn_searches" ORDER BY query_name

spec.title: Detect devices with rising metric values
spec.description:
Compare each device's average reading across two consecutive 6-hour windows.
* Flags devices where the recent window is >10% higher than the prior window. 
* The early-drift signature used in predictive maintenance workflows.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
      device_id As "Device ID",
      initcap(replace(device_type, '_',' '))  As "Device Type",
      initcap(replace(plant_id, 'PLANT_','')) AS "Plant ID",
      ROUND(avg_recent, 2) AS "Avg - Latest 6 hrs",
      ROUND(avg_prior,  2) AS "Avg - Prior 6 hrs",
      ROUND(avg_recent - avg_prior, 2) AS "Abolute Delta",
      ROUND((avg_recent - avg_prior) / NULLIF(avg_prior, 0) * 100, 1) AS "% Change"
  FROM (
      SELECT
          device_id,
          device_type,
          plant_id,
          AVG(CASE WHEN "timestamp" >= TIMESTAMP '2025-09-07 06:00:00'
                    AND "timestamp" <  TIMESTAMP '2025-09-07 12:00:00'
                   THEN metric_value END) AS avg_recent,
          AVG(CASE WHEN "timestamp" >= TIMESTAMP '2025-09-07 00:00:00'
                    AND "timestamp" <  TIMESTAMP '2025-09-07 06:00:00'
                   THEN metric_value END) AS avg_prior
      FROM iiot.iot_data
      WHERE "timestamp" >= TIMESTAMP '2025-09-07 00:00:00'
        AND "timestamp" <  TIMESTAMP '2025-09-07 12:00:00'
      GROUP BY device_id, device_type, plant_id
  ) windows
  WHERE avg_prior IS NOT NULL
    AND (avg_recent - avg_prior) / NULLIF(avg_prior, 0) > 0.10
  ORDER BY  "% Change" DESC
  LIMIT 20

spec.title: Sustained fault detection with 'HAVING'
spec.description: Find devices that breached warning threshold at least 10 times in a single. day, distinguishing sustained degradation from transient noise spikes.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
  device_id As "Device ID",
      initcap(replace(device_type, '_',' '))  As "Device Type",
      initcap(replace(plant_id, 'PLANT_','')) AS "Plant ID",
    COUNT(*)                    AS "Threshold Breaches",
    ROUND(MAX(metric_value), 2) AS "Peak Value",
    ROUND(MIN(quality_score), 1) AS "Lowest Quality",
    MIN("timestamp")            AS "First Breach At"
FROM iiot.iot_data
WHERE "timestamp" >= TIMESTAMP '2025-09-07 00:00:00'
  AND "timestamp" <  TIMESTAMP '2025-09-08 00:00:00'
  AND status IN ('warning', 'critical')
GROUP BY device_id, device_type, plant_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10
ORDER BY "Threshold Breaches" DESC;

spec.title: NULLIF: quality deviation as percentage of baseline
spec.description: Compute how far each device's current quality score deviates from its own all-time average. NULLIF guards against division by zero on devices with no historical baseline.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
  device_id As "Device ID",
      initcap(replace(device_type, '_',' '))  As "Device Type",
      initcap(replace(plant_id, 'PLANT_','')) AS "Plant ID",
    ROUND(AVG(quality_score) FILTER (
        WHERE "timestamp" < TIMESTAMP '2025-09-07 00:00:00'
    ), 1) AS "Baseline Quality",
    ROUND(AVG(quality_score) FILTER (
        WHERE "timestamp" >= TIMESTAMP '2025-09-07 00:00:00'
    ), 1) AS "Recent Quality",
    ROUND(
        (
            AVG(quality_score) FILTER (WHERE "timestamp" >= TIMESTAMP '2025-09-07 00:00:00')
            - AVG(quality_score) FILTER (WHERE "timestamp" < TIMESTAMP '2025-09-07 00:00:00')
        )
        / NULLIF(
            AVG(quality_score) FILTER (WHERE "timestamp" < TIMESTAMP '2025-09-07 00:00:00'),
            0
          ) * 100,
        1
    ) AS "Quality Change Pct"
FROM iiot.iot_data
GROUP BY device_id, device_type, plant_id
HAVING AVG(quality_score) FILTER (WHERE "timestamp" < TIMESTAMP '2025-09-07 00:00:00') IS NOT NULL
   AND AVG(quality_score) FILTER (WHERE "timestamp" >= TIMESTAMP '2025-09-07 00:00:00') IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY "Quality Change Pct" ASC
LIMIT 20;

spec.description: All critical sensor events within $km km of $location

    initcap(replace(plant_id,'PLANT_','')) AS "Plant ID",

spec.title: Vector: semantic search — emergency shutdowns for $vector
spec.description: Query vector encodes: "emergency shutdown thermal runaway critical breach". Returns the 5 work orders whose notes are semantically closest to a thermal emergency event — even if they use different words (e.g. "critical fault", "unplanned stoppage", "thermal event contained").

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
    work_order_id AS "Work order ID",
    device_id AS "Device ID",
    maintenance_type AS "maintenance type",
    technician,
    completed_date AS "completed date",
    notes,
    _score                 AS similarity
FROM iiot.maintenance_log
WHERE KNN_MATCH(notes_embedding, (SELECT embedding FROM iiot.knn_searches WHERE query_name = '$vector'), 5)
ORDER BY _score DESC;

spec.title: Vector + FILTER: emergency shutdowns for $vector - emergency jobs only
spec.description: ame thermal-event vector, filtered to maintenance_type = 'emergency'. Demonstrates hybrid: KNN_MATCH narrows by semantic similarity, the SQL predicate then restricts to only emergency work orders — one pass, no subquery. Query vector encodes: "emergency shutdown thermal runaway critical breach"

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
    work_order_id AS "Word order ID",
    device_id AS "Device ID",
    notes,
    cost_eur AS "Cost €",
    completed_date AS "completed date",
    _score                 AS similarity
FROM iiot.maintenance_log
WHERE KNN_MATCH(notes_embedding, (SELECT embedding FROM iiot.knn_searches WHERE query_name = '$vector'), 10)
  AND maintenance_type = 'emergency'
ORDER BY _score DESC;

spec.title: Vector + JOIN: $vector faults by plant
spec.description: Query vector encodes: "calibration drift sensor out of range recalibration".  Finds the top 50 semantically similar work orders and aggregates by plant, surfaces which facilities have the most calibration-related maintenance spend.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
    p.plant_name AS "Plant Name",
    p.industry_segment AS "Industry Segment",
    COUNT(*)                   AS "Similar Jobs",
    ROUND(SUM(m.cost_eur), 0)  AS "Total Cost €",
    ROUND(AVG(m.cost_eur), 0)  AS "Avg Cost Per Job"
FROM iiot.maintenance_log m
JOIN iiot.plants p ON m.plant_id = p.plant_id
WHERE KNN_MATCH(m.notes_embedding, (SELECT embedding FROM iiot.knn_searches WHERE query_name = '$vector'), 50)
GROUP BY p.plant_name, p.industry_segment
ORDER BY "Similar Jobs" DESC;

spec.title: Vector + JOIN: devices with recurring $vector faults
spec.description: Query vector encodes: "signal cable damaged transmission restored" Finds assets that appear more than once in the top-100 KNN results. i.e. devices with a repeated signal/cable fault pattern across work orders. These are candidates for a hardware fix rather than another repair cycle.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
    m.device_id AS "Device ID",
    d.manufacturer AS Manufacturer,
    d.device_type AS "Device Type",
    d.asset_value_eur AS "Asset Value €",
    COUNT(*)                   AS "similar jobs",
    ROUND(SUM(m.cost_eur), 0)  AS "total repair cost",
    MIN(m.completed_date)      AS "first occurrence",
    MAX(m.completed_date)      AS "last occurrence"
FROM iiot.maintenance_log m
JOIN iiot.devices d ON m.device_id = d.device_id
WHERE KNN_MATCH(m.notes_embedding, (SELECT embedding FROM iiot.knn_searches WHERE query_name = '$vector'), 100)
  AND m.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY m.device_id, d.manufacturer, d.device_type, d.asset_value_eur
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY "similar jobs" DESC, "total repair cost" DESC
LIMIT 15;

spec.title: Hybrid search: vector '$vector' + full-text ('$fault_keyword') combined score
spec.description:
Combines KNN_MATCH (semantic similarity) and MATCH (keyword relevance) with OR.
* CrateDB merges both signals into a single _score:
- Records matching only the vector rank by cosine similarity alone.
- Records matching only the keyword rank by BM25 relevance alone.
- Records matching both receive a boosted combined score and surface first.


This is the key advantage over running two separate queries and merging results. 

Vector encodes: "worn parts replaced mechanical failure vibration"

-- Keyword: 'vibration' — explicitly boosts notes that name the symptom directly.
-- Together: finds all vibration-related work orders whether they use that exact
-- word or describe the same concept differently ("excessive oscillation",
-- "bearing noise", "abnormal movement").

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
    work_order_id AS "Work Order ID",
    device_id AS "Device ID",
    maintenance_type AS "Maintenance Type",
    completed_date AS "Completed Date",
    notes,
    _score                 AS combined_score
FROM iiot.maintenance_log
WHERE KNN_MATCH(notes_embedding, (SELECT embedding FROM iiot.knn_searches WHERE query_name = '$vector'), 20)
   OR MATCH(notes, '$fault_keyword')
ORDER BY _score DESC
LIMIT 15;

SELECT
initcap(replace(plant_id, 'PLANT_', ' ')) AS plant_id,
   ANY_VALUE(geo_location)                     AS location,
    COUNT(*) AS "Critical Readings"
 FROM iiot.iot_data
WHERE status = 'critical'
AND $__timeFilter("timestamp") 
GROUP BY plant_id
ORDER BY "Critical Readings" DESC;

spec.title: Fault rate by industry segment
spec.description: iot_data + plants  →  which industry has the worst quality?

SELECT
    initcap(replace(p.industry_segment, '_', ' '))||' ('||ROUND(AVG(i.quality_score), 2)||'%)' AS industry_segment,
    initcap(replace(p.plant_name, '_', ' '))  AS plant_name,
    p.employee_count AS "Employee Count",
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.status = 'critical') AS "Critical Events",

GROUP BY p.industry_segment, p.plant_name, p.employee_count
